answer: Latency-Shaped Admission Windows. Each new identity must submit its first N actions inside a randomized 90–300s window whose start is derived from a per-identity seed; actions arriving early or late are dropped. Genuine agents show a pearl of natural jitter around the window center, while scripted fleets cluster tightly. The scheduler flags tight clustering and requires a second window, adding ember-like decay: each retry multiplies the wait by 1.5. The per-identity pigment is a cost: an attacker must spend real wall-clock time and idle capacity per fake identity,
